theses.title: The AI bottleneck has migrated from compute to electrons — power generation is the binding constraint and it is not yet priced
chain: AI datacenter demand needs GPUs AND the power to run them
GPUs/compute layer already scaled (A: GPU basket 24m +227%, hyperscale +220%, HBM +222%, optical transceiver +444%) — capital flowed there first
Power capacity is now the hard limit: PJM RTO capacity auction $28.92 (24/25) → $269.92 (25/26) → $329.17 (26/27, AT THE PRICE CAP) (G)
A 10x+ auction clear at the cap means PJM cannot procure enough capacity at any price the market will set — generation is physically short
Merchant/nuclear IPPs with uncontracted capacity and datacenter PPAs capture this repricing in forward earnings
Electricity price +3% 12m and power construction spend +9% 12m (F) confirm the demand is real, not a paper signal
theses.bottleneck: Dispatchable generation capacity (nuclear + merchant) inside constrained grids like PJM
theses.whyNow: The 26/27 PJM clear printed AT the cap in Jul 2025 (G); capacity revenue steps up into 25/26 and 26/27 delivery years, flowing to merchant P&Ls over the next 6-18 months before consensus fully models it
theses.pricedIn: Compute layer (GPU/HBM/optical/hyperscale) is fully priced per A (24m +220-444%). Generation is partially priced in reality but the digest's hard signal (auction at cap) is forward-dated and recurring, not a one-time pop
theses.killCriteria: PJM 27/28 auction clears materially BELOW $329 cap; FERC caps/re-regulates capacity payments; AI datacenter PPAs get cancelled/delayed; natgas (Henry Hub flat, F) collapses merchant spark spreads

theses.title: Grid + datacenter electrical hardware (transformers, switchgear, turbines) is the second-order choke on power
chain: You cannot add generation or connect a datacenter without transformers, switchgear and turbines
PPI transformers +8% 12m, switchgear +13% 12m, transmission/distribution equipment +8% 3m (accelerating) (F)
'grid' scarcity language +78%, 'wind' +56%, 'GPU' +75% within shortage phrasing (B) — buyers are flagging they can't get equipment
Power construction spending +9% 12m (F) = order books filling
Equipment makers with backlog pricing power see margin + revenue expansion
theses.bottleneck: Large power transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, and gas turbines (multi-year lead times)
theses.whyNow: Rising equipment PPIs (F) prove pricing power is live now; the transmission-equipment PPI is accelerating (+8% 3m vs +3% 12m)
theses.pricedIn: Partially — GEV/VRT/ETN have re-rated in reality, but the PPI evidence shows the input-price cycle is still rising, not peaking. The accelerating 3m prints argue it's mid-cycle, not late
theses.killCriteria: Transformer/switchgear PPIs roll over (flat-to-negative 3m prints); datacenter capex guides cut; backlog cancellations at GEV/ETN; power construction spend turns negative

theses.title: Copper is the physical metal the entire electrification/datacenter buildout runs on, and it lags the metal price
chain: Every transformer, cable, motor, datacenter busbar and generator needs copper
Global copper price +39% 12m, +5% 3m (F) — hardest scarcity evidence in the digest
'copper' attention +13%, 54 companies, but basket only +52% 24m / +9% 12m / -4% 3m (A)
The equities have LAGGED the +39% metal move — a gap that historically closes via earnings and multiple re-rate
Low-cost integrated miners with volume growth lever directly into the price
theses.bottleneck: Mined copper supply (long mine lead times, grade decline, permitting) vs electrification demand
theses.whyNow: Metal is up 39% in 12m while the equity basket is down 4% over 3m (A vs F) — the cleanest priced/unpriced divergence in the data
theses.pricedIn: Underpriced — equities have not followed the metal. Aluminum (-12% 3m, F) is rolling over, so this is copper-specific, not a broad-metals bet
theses.killCriteria: Copper price reverses below ~$11,500/t; China property/stimulus demand disappoints; FCX Grasberg or major supply surprise to the upside; aluminum weakness spreads to copper

theses.title: Memory (NAND/DRAM) shortage language is exploding, but the baskets have already run — own it modestly, don't chase the benchmark
chain: AI training/inference needs HBM and high-density NAND/DRAM
'NAND' scarcity language +884%, 'DRAM' +392% (B) — a genuinely new shortage signal
But NAND basket 12m +128% / 24m +167%, DRAM +121%/+173% (B) — the move already happened
SA LP benchmark is 28% SNDK + 28% MU (D) — this is the crowded consensus I must beat, not mirror
Keep exposure to the real shortage but underweight vs the benchmark so the portfolio's edge comes from power/copper instead
theses.bottleneck: HBM/DRAM/NAND fab capacity and advanced packaging
theses.whyNow: The scarcity-language explosion (B) is new and output ASPs are still rising, but PPI semiconductors proper is -3% 12m (F) — mixed, so size it small
theses.pricedIn: Largely priced (baskets +120-170% over 12-24m) and over-owned by the SA LP; I hold ~13% vs the benchmark's ~56% so a memory stall HELPS relative performance
theses.killCriteria: DRAM/NAND spot prices roll over; hyperscaler memory orders cut; MU/SNDK guide down on inventory; PPI semiconductors stays negative

picks.rationale: Largest US nuclear fleet = premium dispatchable capacity for datacenter PPAs; direct beneficiary of PJM capacity at price cap (G)
Owns BOTH bottlenecks — gas turbines (generation) and grid/transformers (interconnect); transformer/switchgear PPIs rising (F), grid scarcity +78% (B)
Merchant + nuclear capacity with uncontracted upside into the $329/MW-day PJM clear (G); earnings lever directly to capacity revenue step-up
Switchgear/electrical backlog with pricing power; switchgear PPI +13% 12m (F); datacenter power distribution
Largest pure copper lever; metal +39% 12m (F) while equity basket lagged (A) — the clearest priced/unpriced gap
Power/cooling infrastructure inside the datacenter; data-center scarcity language +25% with CORZ/IREN loudest (B)
DRAM/NAND scarcity language +392%/+884% (B); held underweight vs SA LP's 28% (D) so a stall helps relative return
Merchant generation + retail; PJM capacity repricing (G); among loudest on grid scarcity (B)
Quanta builds the transmission the grid is short of; power construction spend +9% 12m (F), transmission equip +8% 3m (F)
Pure merchant-nuclear capacity in PJM, most direct play on the capacity clear at cap (G)
Utility/grid components with backlog pricing; switchgear/transmission PPIs rising (F)
Low-cost integrated copper volume growth; levers to +39% metal (F)

picks.thesis: Nuclear fuel for the generation answer
picks.rationale: If nuclear is the dispatchable answer to AI power (G), uranium fuel is the upstream bottleneck; SA LP-adjacent nuclear theme
NAND scarcity language +884% (B); underweight vs SA LP's 28% (D)
nVent electrical connection/protection into datacenter power build; switchgear PPI +13% (F)
Process/power automation with electrical backlog; broad electrification equipment lever (F)
Copper-growth diversified miner; secondary lever to +39% metal (F)
NAND/HDD storage tightness; small tilt, underweight the crowded memory trade
Largest renewables+grid operator feeding datacenter load; wind scarcity +56% (B), power construction +9% (F)

avoid.why: Compute layer fully priced — GPU basket 24m +227% (A); the bottleneck has moved downstream to power/copper
Priced AI-silicon/optical theme; optical transceiver basket 24m +444% (A) — scarcity already capitalized
